statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail adds a point because NQ has drifted back to within 16 points of the 30,704.50 overnight low after a third hour inside the same 108.50-point band, so the containment read is intact but the invalidation level is closer than it was. Stress is unchanged at an elevated 50 on a 5.12% 10-year and October hike odds near 70%.
recommendation: Tail remains below the watch threshold. The published danger window is unchanged at the 24 September U.S. cash open, 13:30 to 15:00 UTC, where opening-auction continuation against an aligned rates backdrop is the structure that would deny retracement. The 12:30 UTC jobless-claims block and the 17:00 UTC seven-year note auction are the secondary checkpoints. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by the mapped state.
headline: Nasdaq-100 futures hold a third hour inside the same overnight band but drift back toward its low as the 10-year stalls near 5.12%
body:
The live Globex path remains the decisive evidence and it still describes a contained, two-way market, though the balance inside that range has shifted. Nasdaq-100 December futures trade 30,720.50, down 44.25 points or 0.14%, quoted at 03:15 UTC, against a 30,780.00 open. The overnight session continues to span the same 108.50-point band between 30,704.50 and 30,813.00, worth 0.35%, now for a third consecutive hour. The difference from the previous hour is position within that band: price sits roughly 16 points above the low and 92 below the high, having given back most of the buy-back that had carried it to mid-range. The structural facts that keep Tail in the low band are unchanged. The 30,704.50 low has not been retested or exceeded, no new session low has printed, and the range has widened on neither edge in three hours. Repeated containment inside an established band is the opposite of the shallow-pullback and failed-retracement structure that Tail measures. The honest caveat is that the single invalidation level is now much closer than it was, which is why Tail adds a point rather than easing further. E-mini S&P 500 futures at 7,761.75, down 0.14% inside a 7,758.50 to 7,779.25 band, track rather than diverge, and that correlation argues the drift is index-wide positioning rather than a Nasdaq-specific impulse.

The rates impulse that drove Wednesday's decline has stalled. The 10-year Treasury yield is quoted 5.12% for 24 September, essentially unchanged on the day, against Wednesday's roughly 16 basis-point surge to a level last seen in July 2007. The 2-year is 4.90%, marginally lower, and the 30-year 5.41%, marginally higher, so the very long end remains the one part of the curve still grinding up while the front end has stopped. That matters for the distinction this assessment turns on: a stalled yield move sustains a difficult environment without supplying the continuous directional pressure a pathological price path would require. The underlying driver is unchanged. September flash PMIs printed far above consensus, with the composite at 58.4, manufacturing at 57.0 and services at 58.7, and Federal Reserve Governor Michael Barr said further policy adjustments are likely needed to bring inflation back to target in a timely fashion. Market-implied odds of a 25 basis point hike on 28 October are quoted near 70%.

Cross-asset evidence remains non-confirming, which is the second reason Tail stays low. WTI trades $91.34, down 0.86%, and Brent $102.16, down 0.89%, extending the pullback from Wednesday's near-4% surge as the market reassesses U.S.-Iran talks at the United Nations, so the second inflation channel is easing rather than compounding the rates channel. VIX closed 15.18, up 6.83% on Wednesday, which is a meaningful daily move from a low absolute level rather than a stress signal in its own right. Asia is split rather than cascading: Japan's Nikkei 225 trades 65,883.41, up 1.33% and itself two-way within a 65,407.37 to 66,249.11 range, while the prior Asian session saw Hong Kong fall about 1% and Shanghai 0.4%. A genuinely aligned global risk-off would not look like this.

Shared Finviz context was read at the start of this run and is not being used as current evidence. Its collection timestamp is 01:41 UTC, roughly 104 minutes before this assessment, which is past the 90-minute freshness boundary, and its collectionStatus is partial with the futures and calendar sections unavailable. Its latest-session breadth, megacap and semiconductor readings are consistent with the Wednesday cash close already described, showing Technology down 0.81%, Semiconductors down 1.67% and five of eight megacaps lower, but they are explicitly non-real-time and cannot establish anything about the current NQ path. The independent research above carries the assessment.

The forward risk is concentrated where it has been all session and it is conditional, not observed. The 12:30 UTC block brings initial and continuing jobless claims alongside the Q2 current account and final August building permits, with Fed speakers at 08:10, 12:00, 12:50 and 14:10 UTC framing it. The danger window stays at the 13:30 to 15:00 UTC cash open, where an opening auction that extends against an aligned long end and produces only shallow pullbacks is the specific structure that would push Tail into the blocking band. That structure has not been observed. The 17:00 UTC seven-year note auction is the secondary checkpoint, relevant through its delayed equity transmission rather than through the auction result itself.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours are fully covered by published Claude assessments. Tail sat between 10 and 12 through the Asian and European hours of 23 September with Stress in the low-to-mid 30s, then stepped up sharply at 14:00 UTC to Tail 25 and Stress 54 as the U.S. cash open met a 16 basis-point surge in the 10-year yield after hot flash PMIs, the one hour in the window that mapped to BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES. Tail then held a 20 to 24 plateau through the U.S. afternoon and into the overnight session, easing to 18 at 01:00 UTC and 17 at 02:00 UTC as Globex settled into a contained range. Those are the opinions published at the time and are not restated with hindsight.
outlookSummary: The published path assumes the overnight band holds and stays in the low Tail band through the Asian and European hours, with Stress easing modestly as the long end stalls. Conditional risk then builds mechanically into the U.S. session: the mapped state reaches WATCH from 11:00 UTC on approach to the jobless-claims block, peaks at Tail 24 in the 14:00 UTC cash hour inside the published danger window, holds a WATCH plateau across the seven-year auction and the afternoon, and decays back to the low band after the 20:00 UTC cash close. Every score beyond the current hour is conditional risk rather than observed structure, and confidence declines with forecast distance. The invalidation for the whole low-Tail path is a decisive break of the 30,704.50 overnight low followed by extension without retracement.
